name: Promo 1: diorama scenes, 16:9 hero slides, launch film and Blender import proof
description: Second round of Meshwright v1 launch material (docs/15 section 7), after comparing our kit with ccore's card: their lead images show assets working together (a playable game, Godot imports) and one rich asset per 16:9 slide, while ours shows many small props. This PRD builds, from our own generated GLBs only: (1) a scene composer that places many GLBs on one plinth as a diorama, (2) two diorama layouts (village, harbour) rendered as a 16:9 still and an orbit, (3) a plinth option for single hero renders, (4) 16:9 hero slides in a film style, (5) a 25-30 s launch film, (6) a Blender headless import check that proves the GLBs import and renders them in Blender. Every image must stay honest: geometry is never edited, dioramas are captioned 'arranged by hand, every object generated by Meshwright v1'.
standingRule: Offline-only PRD. No network, no hf upload, no ollama, no git push, never commit. READ ONLY: runs/imp/distill/*/asset.glb, runs/imp/distill/*/result.json, runs/imp/adaptive/best/glimmer-v3-adaptive/glb/*.glb, bench/glb/briefs.jsonl, bench/distill/briefs.jsonl. WRITE ONLY: scripts/showcase_*.mjs, scripts/promo_film.sh, scripts/blender_import_check.py, release/v1/promo/ (except out/cover_1280x640.png, out/social_1080.png, out/showcase_grid.png, out/how_it_works_1600x640.png, out/turntable_*, out/unfiltered_eval_48.png, which are published and must not change), tests/, docs/15-release.md. Never touch data/, out/ (repo root), eval/, .env, .venv, prompts/. Never modify a GLB's geometry, materials or animation: only position, rotate and uniformly scale whole assets in a scene. Tests use GLBs built in the test (tests/js/glb_util.mjs makeGlb) and temp dirs.
readFirst: scripts/showcase_render.mjs (the studio renderer to extend; keep its CLI and output unchanged)
release/v1/promo/make.mjs (the layout composer and style: dark studio gradient, Avenir Next, accent #9fb3ff) and release/v1/promo/meta.json
tests/js/glb_util.mjs (makeGlb) and tests/js/index.js (how JS tests are registered)
manualGates: Owner looks at every new image and the film before anything is posted or uploaded
Uploading to Hugging Face, posting and committing are done by the owner session after the owner says so

stories.title: Plinth option for single hero renders
stories.description: As the owner, I want a single asset rendered on a low plinth (like ccore's farmyard slide), so a hero shot reads as a finished diorama piece.
steps: scripts/showcase_render.mjs: add `--plinth none|round|square` (default none, which must keep today's output byte-identical for the same inputs) and `--plinth-color HEX` (default 0x9ccf7a top) with `--plinth-side HEX` (default 0x8a5a3c). The plinth is a bevelled slab (top colour for a thin top layer, side colour below) sized 1.25x the asset's footprint (x/z extent), thickness 6% of that size, its top at y = 0, receiving shadows. Frame the camera on asset plus plinth.
Add `--aspect W:H` (default 1:1) so a hero can be rendered 16:9 at `--size` width; keep the asset centred slightly right of centre only when `--offset-x F` is given (default 0).

Tests (tests/js/showcase_render.test.mjs, Chromium): render a makeGlb two-box asset with --plinth none and assert the PNG is identical to a render from before the change (generate the reference in the same test run by calling the default path twice with and without the new flags absent); with --plinth round the PNG differs and has opaque pixels in the bottom band; --aspect 16:9 gives width:height 16:9.
criteria: Default output unchanged (asserted)
Plinth and aspect options produce the asserted image properties
The CLI usage line documents the new flags

stories.title: Scene composer for dioramas (showcase_scene.mjs)
stories.description: As the owner, I want many generated GLBs placed together on one plinth and rendered as one scene, so the material shows assets working together the way ccore's game GIF does.
steps: Create scripts/showcase_scene.mjs `--layout FILE --out DIR [--width 1920 --height 1080] [--frames N] [--name NAME]`. Layout JSON: {plinth: {shape: 'round'|'square', size_m, top, side}, camera: {yaw, pitch, fov, zoom}, items: [{glb, x, z, rot_y_deg, height_m?, scale?}]}. Each item is loaded, its lowest point set to y = 0 (plinth top) and its centre (x/z) moved to (x, z); `height_m` scales it uniformly to that height, otherwise `scale` (default 1, the asset's own metres). Never edit geometry or materials.

Before rendering, check overlaps: compute each placed item's x/z footprint box and print a warning line per overlapping pair (ids and overlap area); `--strict` makes overlaps an error. Print one JSON summary line {items, overlaps, missing}. A missing GLB is an error naming the path.

Lighting, shadows and tone mapping as in showcase_render.mjs (reuse by importing shared code into a small module, scripts/showcase_common.mjs, rather than copying). Still: DIR/NAME.png at width x height on a transparent background. With --frames N: DIR/NAME_orbit/0000.png... a full 360-degree camera orbit around the plinth centre; animated items play their first clip over the orbit.

Tests (Chromium): a layout of three makeGlb assets renders, the summary reports 3 items and 0 overlaps; two items at the same x/z report 1 overlap and fail with --strict; a missing GLB fails with its path; --frames 4 writes 4 frames.
criteria: Overlap, missing-file and strict cases are asserted
Shared lighting code lives in scripts/showcase_common.mjs and showcase_render.mjs output stays unchanged
No GLB geometry or material is modified (asserted by re-parsing a placed GLB's mesh count and material count)

stories.title: Village and harbour diorama layouts
stories.description: As the owner, I want two composed scenes built only from real outputs: a village and a harbour.
steps: Write release/v1/promo/scenes/village.json from these distill ids (runs/imp/distill/<id>/asset.glb): buildings x0022 farm house, x0001 timber cabin, x0004 beach hut is NOT used here; use x0013 stone chapel, x0018 mountain chalet, x0024 water tower, x0005 garden gazebo; nature x0316 broadleaf tree, x0319 ancient oak, x0344 rustling bush, x0336 red toadstool, x0339 log pile; props x0153 lamp post, x0158 supply cart, x0157 wooden signpost, x0149 sack pile, x0146 wheelbarrow; people x0051 hay farmer, x0062 gardener, x0073 waving villager; animals x0121 wagging dog, x0125 paddling duck. Round plinth. Buildings to the back ring, trees between them, props and people in the front half, nothing overlapping (run the composer with --strict until it passes).

Write release/v1/promo/scenes/harbour.json from: x0011 wooden pier, x0019 boat house, x0004 beach hut, g023 lighthouse (runs/imp/adaptive/best/glimmer-v3-adaptive/glb/g023.glb), x0461 fishing trawler, x0462 tugboat, x0460 sailboat, x0465 life raft, x0152 rope coil, x0361 wooden box, x0149 sack pile, x0153 lamp post, x0109 shore crab, x0086 ship crew. Square plinth with a blue 'water' half: a second flat slab (colour 0x5aa0d8, top 1 cm below the land top) under the boats; boats sit on it.

Scale rule: keep real-world metres (scale 1) unless an item is clearly off scale next to the buildings; then set height_m to a plausible real height and record the reason in a `notes` field of that item.

Render each: still 1920x1080 (release/v1/promo/scenes_out/<name>.png) and a 96-frame orbit (release/v1/promo/scenes_out/<name>_orbit/), with --strict passing. Write release/v1/promo/scenes_out/summary.json with each scene's items, ids, overlaps (must be 0) and the per-item scale notes.
criteria: Both layouts pass --strict with 0 overlaps and no missing files (summary.json)
Only GLBs from the listed ids are used
Stills and orbit frames exist at the stated sizes

stories.title: 16:9 hero slides (film style)
stories.description: As the owner, I want 1920x1080 slides that each show one rich subject with a short headline, like ccore's 'A world. Of details.' slide, in our existing dark style.
steps: Extend release/v1/promo/make.mjs with a `--slides` mode (the existing pages keep their exact output when run without it) reading release/v1/promo/slides.json: [{name, kicker, line1, line2, sub, prompt?, image, caption?}]. Layout: left column kicker chip (uppercase, #9fb3ff on a dark pill), line1 white and line2 accent #8fd3ff, both 92px bold, a short rule, sub text, then the prompt in quotes when given; image on the right (trimmed, drop shadow); slide counter 'NN / TT' top right; 'Meshwright v1' bottom right; optional caption under the image in small grey text.

slides.json, 6 slides, images rendered with showcase_render.mjs --plinth round --aspect 1:1 --size 1400 into release/v1/promo/renders_hero/ (create it): 1 village diorama still ('A WORLD.' / 'FROM SENTENCES.', caption 'Arranged by hand. Every object generated by Meshwright v1.'), 2 g012 market stall, 3 x0022 farm house, 4 x0422 mech walker, 5 x0110 octopus, 6 harbour diorama still (same caption rule as 1). Each non-diorama slide shows its exact prompt from release/v1/promo/meta.json (add missing ids to meta.json from runs/imp/distill/<id>/result.json `prompt`).
Write release/v1/promo/out/slides/NN_<name>.png at 1920x1080. Headlines must not claim quality numbers; any number on a slide must be one from docs/15 section 2.
criteria: 6 slides at 1920x1080 exist and the existing out/ images are unchanged (compare hashes before and after in the test or the run log)
Diorama slides carry the 'Arranged by hand' caption
Every prompt shown matches meta.json exactly

stories.title: Launch film (promo_film.sh)
stories.description: As the owner, I want a 25-30 s 1920x1080 MP4 that strings the slides, the diorama orbits and the turntable together, for X, LinkedIn and YouTube.
steps: Create scripts/promo_film.sh using ffmpeg only: sequence = title card (release/v1/promo/out/cover_1280x640.png scaled and padded to 1920x1080, 2.5 s) -> village orbit (frames from scenes_out/village_orbit, 20 fps, composited over the dark studio gradient image release/v1/promo/bg_1920x1080.png which the script renders once via make.mjs or an ffmpeg gradient) -> slides 2-5 (2.5 s each, slow 4% zoom-in) -> harbour orbit -> turntable_1200.mp4 centred on the gradient (3 s) -> end card (slide 1 text replaced by the Ollama command and 'Apache 2.0 · Built on Muse Glimmer 30B', 3 s). 0.4 s crossfades between parts. H.264, yuv420p, CRF 18, faststart, no audio track.
Output release/v1/promo/out/film/meshwright_v1_film.mp4 plus a 1080x1080 centre-cropped variant meshwright_v1_film_square.mp4. Print the duration (must be 25-30 s).

`--dry-run` prints the ffmpeg command lines without running them. Test (tests/py/test_promo_film.py) runs --dry-run against a temp dir of dummy PNGs and asserts the part order, the crossfade count and that no network URL appears.
criteria: Both MP4s exist, 1920x1080 and 1080x1080, 25-30 s (ffprobe output recorded in notes)
Dry-run test asserts order and crossfades
No audio stream (ffprobe)

stories.title: Blender import proof (blender_import_check.py)
stories.description: As the owner, I want proof that the GLBs import into a real 3D tool, like ccore's Godot screenshots, made headless so it is repeatable.
steps: Create scripts/blender_import_check.py, run as `blender -b --factory-startup --python scripts/blender_import_check.py -- --glbs FILE[,FILE...] --report FILE [--render FILE --layout release/v1/promo/scenes/village.json]`. For each GLB: reset to an empty scene, `bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf`, record ok/error, object count, mesh count, total triangles (evaluated), material count and action (animation) count. Write a JSON report with one row per GLB and totals.

With --render: import every item of the layout, place it as the layout says (same placement rules as showcase_scene.mjs), add a sun light and a camera matching the layout camera, and render one EEVEE (or Workbench if EEVEE is unavailable headless) 1920x1080 image. Also write a second image that looks like Blender: Workbench render with the default grey studio look and the outliner-style list of imported object names drawn as a text overlay is NOT needed; instead render Workbench with 'random' object colours so separate parts are visible.

Run it on all GLBs used by the two layouts and the six slides; write release/v1/promo/out/blender/report.json, blender_village_eevee.png and blender_village_parts.png. If blender is not on PATH, the script's wrapper test is skipped with a clear message (do not fail the gate).
Test (tests/py/test_blender_import_check.py): when blender exists, import one makeGlb-equivalent tiny GLB written by the test (two boxes, one animation) and assert ok, mesh count 2, action count 1.
criteria: report.json lists every GLB with ok true or a specific error (any failure is reported, not hidden)
Both Blender renders exist at 1920x1080
The test passes or is skipped only because blender is missing

Run `bash scripts/check.sh` and fix anything it reports in files this PRD owns.
criteria: docs/15 section 7 and LAUNCH.md list every new file
The 'arranged by hand' and 'curated' notes are present
bash scripts/check.sh passes
